audit.title: SmartData

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Opens with "Chainlink SmartData is a suite of onchain data offerings…"; each feed section leads with a definition. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; 12 headings, 0 level skips, no section over 248 words. Weakness: 0 tables — the two feed types and three product categories are natural comparison-table material an engine could lift as a justification unit.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Only 5 numerals/1k words, 0 with units, and vague quantifiers "various," "some" present. No supported networks, decimals, update frequencies, or heartbeat/deviation parameters.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Good. 2 external links to primary sources (`github.com` interface contracts); heavy internal linking to addresses/API reference.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Strong. NAV "calculated by subtracting total liabilities from the total assets held within the vehicle"; AUM and SmartData each get a liftable one-liner.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags. (Head metadata could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read.)

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Single `sol` block includes SPDX, pragma `0.8.24`, import, address, network comment, and full `latestRoundData` destructuring. The "SPDX/WBTC never assigned" flag is a false positive (both appear in comments/license).

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Moderate. Covers what/types/how-to-read, but no troubleshooting or error-string sections, and no MVR runnable code inline (links out). Missing "how do I read a Proof of Reserve feed" style headings.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Consistent product naming; unambiguous prose. Only minor drag from vague quantifiers.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured overview page for Chainlink SmartData that opens with a strong self-contained definition and defines each sub-product (PoR, NAVLink, SmartAUM) crisply. Its biggest strength is answer-first prose with solid internal linking and one complete, runnable Solidity example. Its biggest opportunity is machine-readability — no JSON-LD, canonical, or freshness signals were served — followed by thin concrete specifics (no supported-network lists, update parameters, or decimals) and no symptom/how-to phrased headings to win retrieval. Honest verdict: a solid Good page whose extractable prose is undercut by missing metadata and low quantitative density.

recommendations.title: Add page metadata: JSON-LD `TechArticle`, canonical, and last-updated
recommendations.change: Emit a `TechArticle` JSON-LD block with `headline`, `dateModified`, `inLanguage`, and a self-referential `canonical` URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals let engines parse, date, and trust the page; currently none are present.

recommendations.title: Add a feed-type / product comparison table
recommendations.issue: "0 table(s)" — types and categories are described in prose only.
recommendations.change: Add a table with columns Feed | Interface | Read method | Value type | Example use, rows for Single-value (`AggregatorV3Interface`) and MVR (`BundleAggregatorProxy`), plus PoR/NAVLink/SmartAUM rows.
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract reasons and build justified side-by-side answers; the distinctions are the most-queried aspect.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/how-to phrased headings
recommendations.issue: Headings are concept-titled ("Using Single-value SmartData Feeds") not question-shaped.
recommendations.change: Add H3s like "How do I read a Proof of Reserve feed in Solidity?" and "How do I decode an MVR feed's `latestBundle()` bytes?" mirroring how devs/agents query.
recommendations.why: Question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses even when the answer is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics: networks, decimals, units
recommendations.where: Proof of Reserve, NAVLink, SmartAUM sections
recommendations.issue: "0 [numerals] with units" and vague "answers in units of measurement such as ounces (oz)…"
recommendations.change: State supported networks, typical `decimals()` return, and that PoR answers are `int256` scaled by decimals; give one concrete example (e.g. WBTC PoR reports in BTC, 8 decimals).
recommendations.why: Quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

recommendations.title: Name the common-but-wrong read pattern as a Don't
recommendations.issue: Text says MVR "require a different approach" but doesn't guard against the generic prior.
recommendations.change: Add a Don't: "Do not call `latestRoundData()` on MVR feeds — use `latestBundle()` and decode the bytes array." Lead the section with the canonical `BundleAggregatorProxy`/`latestBundle()` API.
recommendations.why: Skimming engines default to the ubiquitous `latestRoundData` prior; naming the wrong call prevents confident inversions.

recommendations.title: Inline a minimal MVR read snippet
recommendations.issue: Only links out; no runnable MVR example on-page ("languages: [sol]" = single block).
recommendations.change: Add a short, complete Solidity snippet showing `latestBundle()` + `abi.decode` into a struct, or a labeled excerpt, so agents get the pattern without a second fetch.
recommendations.why: Complete on-page snippets raise agent-runnability; a link-only section can't be lifted.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers
recommendations.where: "bundle multiple data points of various types," "In some instances"
recommendations.change: Enumerate the types (numeric + string/bytes/bool) and state the specific composite-adapter case.
recommendations.why: Precise enumeration is more quotable than qualitative hedges.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers: "various types," "In some instances" — minor.
Two "(Image: Image)" placeholders — alt text/captioning absent, so the image content is invisible to engines; add descriptive alt text.
No stale-content risk detected in prose, but absence of any dateModified means freshness cannot be signaled at all.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this page is listed in it.
Site-level JSON-LD/canonical templating likely governs the missing metadata; fix at the template level, not just this page.
Head metadata could not be verified from the provided content — pass raw `<head>` to the CLI to confirm og/canonical status before treating as truly absent.
